method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md. Ran atomscan slow with updates/reference fetching disabled and cleave facts for every specimen. Reverse-engineered local bytes with Rizin, ILSpy, PE/CLR parsers, AutoIt-Ripper and binary-refinery. No specimen was executed. Fetched referenced documentation, signing CRL, sandbox reports and a release MSI for independent corroboration.

samples.identification: AutoIt-marked opaque carrier with arithmetic-encoded executable configuration
samples.confidence: Limited: likely malicious carrier; final payload and activation unresolved
evidence: The 498759-byte file is data, not a PE. Both filefacts and binwalk find no executable container; scanning every raw MZ occurrence with a PE parser finds no valid embedded PE.
AU3!EA06 occurs at 71113 and 498751. The clear delimiter at 71121 encloses 90 bytes whose values minus 120 modulo 256 produce a coherent delimiter-separated configuration.

Decoded configuration: 4\@/T\@/System\@/svchost.exe.exe\@/4\@/4\@/System\@/0\@/SVCHOST.EXE\@/4\@/\@/1\@/4\@/4\@/1. Clear framing continues with nothing. The field boundaries, executable suffix and values all obey the same transform.
The two opaque regions at 0..71113 and 71227..498751 have entropies approximately 7.9971 and 7.9995. These measurements and EA06 markers are neutral properties, not independent hostile behaviors.

AutoIt-Ripper reports no standard EA05/JB01 location chunk and recovers no script; binary-refinery's a3x unpacker recovers no member. Single-byte XOR/additive whole-file transforms do not recover an MZ start. There is no recovered execution path or URL to follow.

The deliberately concealed executable configuration and opaque two-part carrier tip the balance toward malicious packaging. No claimed process launch, persistence, injection, C2, payload family or successful activation is justified.
samples.coverage_gap: Only one suspicious behavior is independently supported: nested arithmetic concealment. The minimum of two suspicious behaviors cannot be met without duplicating that observation or inventing opaque payload behavior.
samples.classifier_disagreement: Calibrated classifier remains benign (level -1, class 0); analyst judges the carrier likely malicious. No inaccurate or duplicate traits were added to raise its score.
samples.marker: Opaque carrier: shifted svchost config; entropy made notable

samples.balance: Byte-identical release component and coherent file-manager paths outweigh the malware-corpus label. Revoked signing and abuse potential remain accurate findings; deployment authorization is unknown.
evidence: ILSpy decompilation and independent parsing of all 35 CLR method bodies succeeded. No managed resources or appended data after the certificate table. Assembly references name version-matched ScreenConnect.Core and ScreenConnect.Windows plus ordinary .NET libraries.
Main initializes exception logging, WinForms and DLL-search hardening. Referenced release helpers show FixupAppDomain is empty; FixupProcess sets System32 DLL search and an image-load mitigation.

GETMESSAGE and CALLWNDPROCRET hooks are restricted to the current thread. They redirect mouse-wheel events and customize file-picker context menus. WinEvent hooks customize the file-picker icon, tree expansion, controls and layout; this is not keyboard surveillance.
The program reads the ProfileList ProfilesDirectory registry value, initializes an IFileOpenDialog, selects filesystem/show-hidden options and displays ScreenConnect File Manager.

DialogEventHandler.OnFileOk obtains the selected filesystem path and calls Process.Start(new ProcessStartInfo(path) { UseShellExecute = true }). This is a user-selection launch surface. No fixed command, relay configuration, embedded payload, persistence registration or remote task is supplied.

The freshly fetched 128835584-byte release MSI has SHA256 0dabef8ee019bc34bf315794df0f5321ee8122e18d87411ab5f79f6ef73f46a0. Extracted member filC1D18007D3175279B0EDD654D18B0CA5 exactly matches the specimen SHA256.

Authenticode content digest and signer cryptography are intact. A fresh DigiCert CRL, whose signature was independently verified, lists serial 0B9360051BCCF66642998998D5BA97CE with key_compromise and revocation date 2022-08-17. The existing suspicious compromised-signer trait is retained.

Triage static score 8 consists of revoked-certificate/untrusted-signer findings. The behavioral report score is 3, launching this file and dw20 .NET crash reporting. Its shown Google PKI flows have unrelated process IDs; no ScreenConnect C2 is established by those flows.

Far-future COFF/debug values coexist with a reproducible-build marker and are preserved as raw metadata. Collector filename mismatch and standard SkipVerification metadata do not establish deception or exploitation.
samples.source_label_explanation: Direct evidence supports revoked signing as the sandbox trigger; AV names also explicitly classify RemoteAdmin/HackTool/Unwanted behavior. Collection alongside malicious use remains possible, but the supplied standalone component does not supply that deployment context.

samples.balance: Traced interpreter and runtime operations explain the capabilities; no supplied hostile script, fixed command or alternate payload path was found. This does not establish how the interpreter was deployed.
evidence: Rizin traces CRT startup to main at 0x461b50. Main creates a Lua state through 0x41a0a0, supplies the interpreter callback 0x4021a0 to protected call 0x40c3a0, handles errors and closes state through 0x406060.

The callback parses normal -e/-l/-b/-j/-O/-E options, initializes libraries and arguments, reads LUA_INIT with getenv at 0x40279b, and branches between evaluating supplied source and loading a file when the value starts with @. Script argument handling and REPL paths match LuaJIT's documented purpose.

At 0x44e370, the os.execute wrapper obtains a caller-provided argument and passes it to C system at 0x44e398. The io.popen wrapper similarly passes Lua arguments to _popen at 0x44d2d0. No fixed shell command is supplied by the executable.

Executable-memory operations include LuaJIT machine-code protection management at 0x429f30 and MinGW pseudo-relocation permission changes at 0x45f030. The 0x40 third-argument finding corresponds to a genuine local VirtualProtect call at 0x45f102.
TLS callbacks 0x45ee50 and 0x45ee00 dispatch ordinary TLS initialization/cleanup at 0x45f750, including critical-section setup and registered cleanup, not a recovered payload entry.
Imports, FFI/library resolution, thread creation, process termination, TEB reads, native PE walks and executable memory are dual-use interpreter/runtime capabilities and remain notable.

The entire apparent overlay is accounted for by 129 COFF symbols (2322 bytes) and the 2371-byte string table: 506368 + 2322 + 2371 = 511061, exactly EOF. No appended archive or custom bytecode payload is recovered; PE exports are absent.

The visible URL is the LuaJIT project banner. Its homepage and official source/documentation were fetched. No network API import, fixed callback host, script sidecar or dependency download is supplied. Future-valued timestamp and absent ASLR are preserved packaging facts; the exact upstream binary build is not asserted.
samples.source_label_explanation: The sole AV name says MisusedLegit.LuaJIT, consistent with an interpreter collected from a malicious script bundle. Missing companion scripts and launch context prevent attributing their behavior to this executable. A rare corpus mislabel is another possibility.
missing_context: Original package and actual operator intent
samples.marker: LuaJIT 2.1: standard interpreter paths; no hostile script supplied

yaml_change.change: Promote component to notable and state the numeric whole-file entropy observation explicitly.
yaml_change.reason: A complete measured property is not an incomplete component fragment. Ordinary compressed archives can satisfy it; the observation asserts neither encryption nor concealment.
yaml_change.invariant: Identical ID, matcher, 7.98 threshold, 262144-byte minimum, format/platform scope, confidence and Chrome-theme exclusion. No removal, narrowing or severity reduction.
yaml_change.consumers: Nine direct references in six files were inspected; none changes. No exact ancestor directory selectors target metadata, metadata/file, metadata/file/data-blob or metadata/file/entropy.
yaml_change.placement_hold: The documented target is metadata/file/entropy. Current validator's BROAD_ARCHIVE_FILETYPE_ALLOWLIST admits this scope only at the old source filename, and archives is not a supported for group. A trial relocation was rejected and fully reverted. Retain the explicitly permitted legacy home pending coordinated engine admission; do not narrow archive coverage to make a move pass.

verification.focused: Seven generated controls pass against baseline and current rules: high entropy data, low entropy, undersized data, ordinary ZIP, encrypted executable-name 7z, header-locked 7z and Chrome theme ZIP. The theme is a valid PNG and manifest; test-rules independently confirms the exclusion. Existing suspicious encrypted-7zaes-windows-exe and hostile header-encrypted-7z-payload remain detected.
verification.broader: Compared 21 file records including archive members and existing binary-entropy-table.zip, high-entropy.dat and does-nothing sample.7z. Zero lost detections. One neutral entropy property becomes visible on the ordinary entropy-table ZIP because notable findings are retained.
verification.sample_findings: Counts remain 16, 78, 64; no sample findings added or removed. Only the carrier's entropy observation changes criticality from 1 to 3.
verification.classifier: All three remain class 0 / level -1. Carrier probability 0.7137588 to 0.71199745; ScreenConnect 0.89942145 unchanged; LuaJIT 0.3152792 unchanged.

does_nothing_fixture_review.change: Explicitly allow this accurate neutral property on this single fixture in testdata/expectations.toml. The existing score cap of 9 is unchanged. No trait suppression or attack allowance.
